title: HCP — Change Entry Categories — payload
description: The request payload of the HCP 2.0-draft-3 Change categories operation (HCP 4.2.1, 4.5, 5.4; `PUT /v2/entries/{entryId}/categories` in HCP 9.2, 9.4.10): a Management Client, acting for the Authorizing Principal, sets an entry's categories, moving it between authorization scopes. HCP defines no schema for this operation; the members come from HCP 9.2 and 9.4.10. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

entryId.description: HCP `entryId` (the `{entryId}` path parameter of HCP 9.2, 9.4.10): the entry's stable `id` (HCP 4.2), by which a Management Client names an entry (HCP 9.4.5).

categories.description: HCP `categories`: the entry's new `classification.categories`, replacing the old list whole (HCP 9.4.10, 4.2.1). One or more, without duplicates (HCP 4.2, 4.5). Each must be a registered category the provider holds or a custom category it supports (HCP 4.5). The maxItems of 256 is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

expectedVersion.description: HCP `expectedVersion`: the `record.version` the Management Client showed the Authorizing Principal. Where it is not the entry's current version, the operation fails with version conflict and changes nothing (HCP 5.4, 5.5).

accessToken.description: The Management Client's HCP access token (HCP 9.3), carried unchanged. HCP's HTTP binding sends it as a Bearer token; this member carries it in the document. The provider validates it exactly as over HTTP and treats it as opaque. The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

Response.title: HCP — Change Entry Categories — response payload
Response.description: The entry, with its new categories (HCP 9.4.10). HCP's result body is the entry itself; the carriage wraps it in `entry`. Failures use trust-task-error, not this shape.

entry.description: The HCP result (HCP 9.4.10): the whole entry, as a Management Client receives it (HCP 7.4), with its new `classification.categories`. Its `record.version` is unchanged: a change of categories creates no version (HCP 4.2.1).
